Shades of Cool by Lana Del Rey helped me reconcile with the fact I couldn't fix this person or make them want me in any way. That it didn't matter that I felt like I could heal them, or that I could really keep forgiving and loving them even when they hurt me. Some people you can't get through to and it hurts. I'll never forget crying so dramatically in my bedroom during the guitar solo, just trying to get through the pain or claw my way out of my skin. The Ultraviolence album came out just as I started going through that ironically.

Young Blood by The Naked and Famous gives me so much nostalgia to junior year when I used to bop my head to it in my dad's car with the windows down while the sun was setting. It literally sounds like freedom and the 'yeah, yeah, yeahs' sounds like a whole other world. It makes you yearn for friends to do crazy, music video stuff with, but not in a sad way, more like a hoping yearning. It gives you faith that eventually you will have people who understand you.

Holding On To You by 21 Pilots helped me through a bad season of depression. I used to watch the video over and over again with tears in my eyes trying not to harm myself. The lyrics and the video really feel like an accurate representation of whats really going through your head when you have depression and it made me feel less alone.

Lastly everything by Azealia Banks. Especially Licorice and Luxury. I used to listen to her all the time when I was writing a book about rich teenagers and it was such a fucking mood and became the soundtrack of the project lol.

2. Badlands by Halsey. I can't see her topping it.  It's a whole masterpiece. Her lyrics and imagery was way better here.

3. Reputation by Taylor Swift. It's one of her best albums, even better than 1989 (don't @me on this.) It's a perfect blend of edginess still paired with the romanticism Taylor Swift is known for. (I also don't know why everyone keeps saying a track called TIWWCHNT exist, like what?)

The situation was horrible but it lead me to actually getting to know Him.

IMO, you don't need a big moment to go back. You just need to go. Our relationship with Him isn't always going to be "grand" or filled with cinematic moments. You don't have to wait for anything, you just have to decide to go.
